# SparseApplyRMSProp

English | [简体中文](./README.md)

| <term>Ascend 950PR&950DT products</term>                     |     √    |
| <term>Atlas A3 products</term>   |    √     |
| <term>Atlas A2 products</term>    |    √     |
| <term>Atlas 200I/500 A2 inference products</term>                      |    ×     |
| <term>Atlas inference products</term>                               |    ×     |
| <term>Atlas training products</term>                               |    ×     |

## Function

- **Operator function**: Performs an update of the RMSProp optimization algorithm on the rows of the specified sparse indexes. According to the indices vector, the operator gathers the corresponding rows from var/ms/mom, applies the RMSProp update formulas, and scatter-writes the updated rows back. Missed rows remain unchanged.

- **Formula**:

For each index `i` in `indices`:

$$
\begin{aligned}
\text{ms}_{\text{new}}[i] &= \rho \cdot \text{ms}_{\text{old}}[i] + (1 - \rho) \cdot \text{grad}[i]^2 \\
\text{mom}_{\text{new}}[i] &= \text{momentum} \cdot \text{mom}_{\text{old}}[i] + \text{lr} \cdot \text{grad}[i] / \sqrt{\text{ms}_{\text{new}}[i] + \epsilon} \\
\text{var}_{\text{new}}[i] &= \text{var}_{\text{old}}[i] - \text{mom}_{\text{new}}[i]
\end{aligned}
$$

## Constraints

- All data tensors (var, ms, mom, lr, rho, momentum, epsilon, grad) must use the same dtype (float16/bfloat16/float32).
- The data type of indices is int32 or int64.
- var.shape == ms.shape == mom.shape.
- grad.shape[0] == indices.shape[0].
- var.shape[1:] == grad.shape[1:], that is, the trailing dimensions of var and grad must match.
- The rank of var is >= 1.
- The rank of indices is 1.
- The values in indices should be in the range [0, var.shape[0]) and should be unique. If indices contains duplicate values, the result is unpredictable (consistent with the TensorFlow behavior).
- When indices is empty (len(indices) == 0), the computation is skipped, and var/ms/mom remain unchanged.
- For fp16/bf16, the internal computation is performed in fp32 and then cast back to the original type.
